JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, the petitioner is working in the Nyamithra Bank,
High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru and was permanent resident of Channapatna Taluk,
Ramanagara.

Further after his work he went to his native place on 03.08.2023 and was about get back to his usual work, he left his house on his bike bearing Reg.No.KA-42-V-5926 at 7.00 a.m to pick up the bus on 05.08.2023, around 7.45 a.m, near to Channapatna- Bevooru road,
Kotamaranahalli Village, Mallur Hobli, Channapatna Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time the 2 nd respondent / rider of the bike bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176 rides his bike and came from opposite direction with high speed, endangering human life dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
As a result of which both petitioner and respondent No.2 along with their bikes fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

It is alleged that after the accident petitioner was shifted to Channapatna Government Hospital, wherein he took first aid and then shifted to Mandya Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.

3. The petitioner alleged that after theis incident on the same day the brother of the petitioner went to jurisdictional Police station to lodge the complaint against the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176.
The concerned police have told that a case has been already registered agaisnt Devaraju, so the they can't register the same complaint for the same accident.
After discharge from the hospital, the petitioner sent the complaint through Post to the S.P, Ramanagara Town, Ramanagara District on 11.08.2023 and also to the jurisdictional police station.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and driver and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1 & 2.
The respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel.
On perusal of order sheet dated 16.02.2024 it reflects that statutory time for filing WS of respondent No.2 is elapsed.
Hence WS of respondent No.2 is taken as not filed.
5. The petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to P26 were marked on his behalf.

Dr. C.A.
Ashok, Oral Maxillofacial surgeon examined as PW.2 and through him got marked Ex.P.27 to 29 documents.
Further the Investigating Officer got examined as PW.3.

7. The following points are raised for consideration :

POINTS 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 05.08.2023, around 7.45 a.m., near Kotamaranahalli village,
Channapatna - Bevooru Road, Madutu Hobli, Channapatna Taluk, Ramanagara due to composite negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-42-V-5926 and motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
8.

My answers to the above points are as follows :-
Point No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:
REASONS 9. POINT NO.1:
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/- together.
The case of the petitioner lies an narrow compass as to claiming of compensation amount for injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.
Before dwelling into analyzing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have the birds eye of the case of petitioner in a nutshell.

10. It is the case of petitioner that, after his work he went to his native place on 03.08.2023 and was about get back to his usual work, he left his house on his bike bearing Reg.No.KA-42- V-5926 at 7.00 a.m to pick up the bus on 05.08.2023, around 7.45 a.m, near to Channapatna- Bevooru road,
Kotamaranahalli Village, Mallur Hobli, Channapatna Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that the 2nd respondent / rider of the bike bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-HE-1176 rides his bike and came from opposite direction with high speed, endangering human life dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle and caused the accident.
As a result of which both petitioner and respondent No.2 along with their bikes fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

It is alleged that after the accident petitioner was shifted to Channapatna Government Hospital, wherein he took first aid and then shifted to Mandya Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.

The petitioner alleged that after this incident on the same day the brother of the petitioner went to jurisdictional Police station to lodge the complaint against the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176.
The concerned police have told that a case has been already registered against Devaraju, so the they can't register the same complaint for the same accident.

sentences.text:
After discharge from the hospital, the petitioner sent the complaint through Post to the S.P,
Ramanagara Town, Ramanagara District on 11.08.2023 and also to the jurisdictional police station.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and driver and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
11. In support of case of petitioner himself stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in- chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 documents.
The petitioner also got examined the doctor who was assessed the disability is examined as PW.2 and through him Ex.P.27 to 29 were marked.
Further more he has also examined the IO who investigated the Crime No.212/2023 as PW.3.
In order to falsify the case of the petitioner the respondent No.1 has not appeared and was placed exparte.
Further the respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel but he failed to contest the matter by filing his written statement.
12. It is vehemently contended by the petitioner that the accident caused because of negligent act of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by wife of injured Kariyappa / rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-HE-1176, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed chargesheet against the petitioner / rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-V-5926 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.

But having regard to the evidence of PW.3 and Ex.P.3 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.5 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the riders of both the motorcyclist.
It is a settled principles of law that the negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
13. Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
. Duty:
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
. Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
. The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her. .
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

sentences.text: Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
14. The facts of this case are not in dispute.
The accident has occurred in the turning spot and the said place is also in the middle of the road.
Charge sheet for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC has been filed against the claimant.
But the said criminal case has been pending.

In the circumstances, the following questions arise for consideration of this Court :
1) Whether the accident has occurred solely due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176 or due to the negligence on the part of both the riders of the motorcyclist ?
2) Whether the claimant is entitled for any compensation ?
15.
In order to prove the contention the petitioner has examined the Investigating Officer in Crime No.212/2023 of Channapatna Rural Police station as PW.3.
In his exmination in chief he stated that after investigation he filed charge sheet.
He stated that the accident is occured between two motorycles.
Further he stated that the accident occured due to the negligence of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-V-5926.

He further stated that, the complainant / injured was proceeding on motorcycle No.KA-05-HE-1176 was traveling on Kotamaranahalli, Bevuru Road when the accused came from Mailanayakanahalli side at the turn and collided with the accident.
He further stated that spot sketch was not prepared.
He further admitted that the accident occurred at the turn.
The accident was in the middle of the road at the turn.
He further stated that the complainant vehicle should have been on the left side but it was in the middle.
The vehicle of the accused should have been on left side but it was also on the middle.
He further admitted that the accident occurred due to the fault of the drivers of both the vehicles.
But the victim i.e., rider of vehicle belongs to complainant was sustained more injuries than the present petitioner.
Therefore he had filed charge sheet against the present petitioner's vehicle.
16. The learned counsel for petitioner has made available a copy of the spot mahazar Ex.P.3 and Motor Vehicle Inspection Report at Ex.P.7.
On perusal of the panchanama reveals that two wheeler of the complainant and another two wheeler of the petitioner in this case dashed against each other while both were negotiating a blind curve.
The spot of the accident is at the turn road, near Channapatna - Bevooru road.
Though the petitioner has been charged with the offence punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC, and the same criminal case is pending before the jurisdictional Criminal Court.
17. The admission of PW.3 categorically reveals that, the accident occurred at the turn.
The accident was in the middle of the road at the turn.
Further the complainant vehicle should have been on the left side but was in the middle.
The vehicle of the accused was also on the middle.
Admittedly it was head and collusion,

He further admitted that the accident occurred due to the fault of the drivers of Devaraju H K vs Krishna N Bhat on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56468931/

sentences.text: The person shown in the charge sheet as victim was sustained more injuries than the present petitioner hence he had indicted only the driver of one person's vehicle as accused and filed the charge sheet.
Hence it is clear that only for the grievous injuries sustained by the complainant he filed charge sheet against this petitioner only.
There is some negligence on the part of the injured motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176 driver, but there is a greater negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
Added more even the charge sheet filed against the petitioner herein and he was arrayed as accused.
No.1. This court is aware of the fact that, charge sheet is not the conclusive proof and the orders of the criminal court will not bind this Tribunal.
From the discussion made supra it is clearly forthcoming that there is a greater negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.

Hence negligence is fixed on the part of petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-V-5926 and rider / complainant in Crime No.212/2023 of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176 & in the ratio of 80 : 20 respectively.
As such, I answer point No.1 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

POINT NO.2 :
18. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
The petitioner has exhibited his DL and Aadhar card at Ex.P.14 & 15 wherein his date of birth is shown as 15.07.1985.
This means that the petitioner was aged (37 years 9 months 24 days) 38 years on the date of accident.
19. The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was working as a Attender at Nyamithra Sahakari Bank Ltd., Bengaluru and thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
However except producing ID card at Ex.P.12, no documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this Court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 05.08.2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

sentences.text: As per the medical records petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Subconjuctval chemosis (L), Restricted mouth opening, tenderness in zygomatic region left, tenderness in angle region of mandible.

The Discharge summary issued by Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences which is marked at Ex.P.18 indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 05.08.2023 to 10.08.2023 (6 days in total).
During the course of treatment he treated with ORIF of angle fracture of mandible on left.
21. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to accidental injuries he became disabled and lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined PW.2-Dr.C.A. Ashok, Oral and Maxillo facial surgeon at MIMS, Mandya, who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him he found that the petitioner has Subconjuctval chemosis (L), Restricted mouth opening, tenderness in zygomatic region left, tenderness in angle region of mandible.
The CT Scan shows : Skull Base with OPD with Angle of Mandible left fracture.

As per the clinical examination conducted by him, he was referred to a higher centre to management of angle facture with of mandible as their department of dentistry does not have the instruments to do it.
Further he stated that the patient was treated or with ORIF of Angle with of mandible on left on 09.08.2024.
Further the lower wisdom tooth on right was removed.
And at the follow up period on 19.11.2023 plate removal was done at private set up due to dehiscence infection in surgical region.

Further on recent examination conducted on 23.07.2024 the petitioner complains of pain on left side of lower jaw, pain on chewing hard food on lower jaw and incidents of numbness on the left side of jaws.

After examination Tenderness on chewing mouth mirror on left side by patient advice QPG- Slight malunion on left angle, he found that petitioner had sustained total permanent disability to Maxillo facial skeleton at 70%.
However, a careful scrutiny of the medical records indicates that the doctor/ PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

22. Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the Physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the Doctor/ PW.2, the possibility of the fact that PW.1 may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 9%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore I consider the functional disability of PW.1 at 9%.

In this backdrop the just &
reasonable compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the following heads :
23.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 6 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take him care by leaving their duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.2,000/- per day and a sum of Rs.12,000/- (2,000 X 6) is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
25. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:

As referred above, considering the nature of injuries, treatment given & duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 4 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.64,000/- (16,000 X 4) under this head.
26. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.19.
As per that he has spent Rs.48,265/- towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the cross-examination of PW.1, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.48,265/- which is rounded off to Rs.48,300/- towards medical expenses.
27. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '15'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.2,59,200/- (Rs.16,000 X 12 X 15 X 9/100) is awarded under this head.

28. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
Unfortunately at the age of 38 years the petitioner has suffered accidental injuries leading to permanent disability in respect of his mandible and maxillo facial skeleton (left and lower jaw).
It is relevant note that the function of jaws is basically to hold the teeth which in turn will help chew the food and for esthetics (appearance).
The doctor witness has opined that with treatment the petitioner will be able to look normal but his ability to bite / chew hard food will be restricted to 70% only.

Under such circumstances certainly there would be some sort of discomfort which would come in the way of the petitioner enjoying the basic pleasure of human life i.e., eating normal food and for that he needs to be compensated suitably.
For the loss that the petitioner shall suffer in this regard ends of justice would be met if he is awarded a compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head..
29. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.
30. EXPENSES INCURRED TOWARDS DAMAGES CAUSED TO THE VEHICLE:
PW.1 has deposed that in the accident his motorcycle was badly damaged and he has spent substantial amount towards its repair.
In order to substantiate this aspect he has produced estimation for damage repair total amounting to Rs.47,375/- at Ex.P.11.
And he was also produced 6-Vehicle bills repair bill issued by Mahalakshmi Automobiles for Rs.23,945/- produced and same is exhibited at Ex.P24.
That is to say, no document has been filed with regard to the actual costs incurred towards repair.
In fact Ex.P24 cash bill is issued after lapse of 9 months from the date accident.

Be that as it Devaraju H K vs Krishna N Bhat on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56468931/

31. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 12,000-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges:
2 Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid- : 64,000-00 up period 4
Medical expenses : 48,300-00 5 Loss of future income due : 2,59,200-00 to disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil -
Total 4,83,500-00 Less 80% towards contributory : 3,86,800-00  negligence on the part of the  petitioner
Total compensation awarded : 96,700-00 32.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
33. The respondent No.1 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
He has not produced any document to show that his vehicle had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.

In the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the accident was caused by the driver of the offending vehicle (respondent No.2 herein), the respondent No.1 is vicariously liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Tribunal.
Hence he is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

Therefore this point is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
34. POINT NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the evidence of PW.3 and Ex.P.3 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.5 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the riders of both the motorcyclist.
It is a settled principles of law that the negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
. The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
The accident has occurred in the turning spot and the said place is also in the middle of the road.
The accident was in the middle of the road at the turn.
Further the complainant vehicle should have been on the left side but was in the middle.
The vehicle of the accused was also on the middle.
He further admitted that the accident occurred due to the fault of the drivers of Devaraju H K vs Krishna N Bhat on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56468931/

The person shown in the charge sheet as victim was sustained more injuries than the present petitioner hence he had indicted only the driver of one person's vehicle as accused and filed the charge sheet.
Hence it is clear that only for the grievous injuries sustained by the complainant he filed charge sheet against this petitioner only.
There is some negligence on the part of the injured motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HE-1176 driver, but there is a greater negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
No.1. This court is aware of the fact that, charge sheet is not the conclusive proof and the orders of the criminal court will not bind this Tribunal.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the Physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the Doctor/ PW.2, the possibility of the fact that PW.1 may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 9%, cannot be ruled out.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
33. The respondent No.1 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
He has not produced any document to show that his vehicle had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.
In the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the accident was caused by the driver of the offending vehicle (respondent No.2 herein), the respondent No.1 is vicariously liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Tribunal.
